scope: The permanent exterior of the Arctic and Antarctic Museum in the former St. Nicholas Edinoverie Church in Saint Petersburg, in its circa-2008 museum configuration. Includes the mapped four projecting fronts, the principal Marata approach, two-tier classical massing and green central dome. The separate chapels, interiors and temporary restoration works are outside this model.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum occupies the former church built from 1820 to 1838. The conversion was undertaken to the design of A. V. Sivkov.
Six-column Doric portico, Doric second tier, and later museum conversion.
The former church’s lower portico has six Doric columns and the upper tier has corner towers joined by colonnades. The central dome caps the cube.
The museum describes an upper gallery beneath the dome and a view over 30 meters above the city. Exact exterior eave and dome heights remain estimated.
